title: The Robbed Coach
subtitle: Wednesday 29 June to Sunday 3 July 1881: The Last Run Out, a Red Rag on a Juniper, a Boy's Sombrero and a Poster by Friday

setting.name: The Albuquerque road, Santa Teresita and Paragon, the first days of July
setting.description: Coach No. 7 makes the Rio Seco line's last scheduled run: Albuquerque to the Puerco crossing on Wednesday, then through the Puerto de Piedra to Santa Teresita on Thursday, then to Plata Vieja on Friday. It never gets past Thursday afternoon. The robbery at the Puerto de Piedra is the opening set piece. After it come the tracks in the arroyo, the dead messenger, the plaza at dark, the inquest, and the Company's town eighteen miles north, where by Friday night a reward poster names a seventeen-year-old vaquero. The scenario ends on Sunday 3 July with Lon Brisbane's funeral and the party knowing that the plaza didn't do it, and suspecting who did.
setting.atmosphere: Heat and distance. The coach rocks on its leather thoroughbraces like a boat. Dust comes in at the curtains, and the passengers sweat in wool and talk to pass the hours. Old Jethro sings to the horses in two languages. At the Puerco station there is coffee, mutton and a fiddle, and nobody quite says it is the last time. Then the basalt gap: black boulders, junipers, a red rag tied to a branch, and the single flat crack of a big rifle. Afterwards the light goes long and gold over the llano, the dead man is laid across the roof seat under a slicker, and the coach rolls into the plaza at a walk while the church bell rings for the dead. In Paragon the band plays on Friday night and the new lumber smells of turpentine.

keyLocations.name: Coach No. 7, la Doña, and the Puerco station
keyLocations.description: A mud-red Concord coach, built in New Hampshire in 1869, with the line's name in gold on the door panels and a painted Santa Teresa on the boot that a plaza girl did in 1872. Six horses. Jethro Petree drives and Lon Brisbane rides shotgun on the box. Rafael Candelaria, the relief driver, rides on the roof with the mail sacks. Nine seats inside. The Puerco station, forty miles out, is an adobe station house with a ramada, corrals and a dug well beside the dry sand bed of the Rio Puerco. The keeper, old Doroteo Griego, has kept it for Ludlow for twelve years and has been offered a job by the Company.
features: The express box: iron-bound oak, chained by a padlocked chain to a ring in the floor of the front boot, under the driver's feet. The driver carries the padlock key on a thong; the messenger has the box key
The passengers: whichever pregens are aboard, Celestino Trujillo going home with a carpet bag of printed People's tickets, and a Kansas City whiskey drummer named Ollie Gruber who talks too much
The Puerco station's ramada at night: a fiddle, mutton and chile, Jethro drinking more than a driver should before a run, and Lon cleaning his shotgun
The Post Office notice and the chalked ¿Y nosotros? on the express office door, which Celestino copies into his notebook
encounters: No combat on Wednesday. A conversation with Jethro Petree, who wants to say something to someone and doesn't
Ollie Gruber, the drummer, who will cheat at cards if anyone plays with him, and is caught at once by a Gambler
secrets: Jethro Petree is the inside man. At the Puerco station after supper he asks Lon Brisbane, twice, to ride inside tomorrow 'out of the sun, an old man's fancy'. Lon laughs and says the messenger's place is on the box. Insight DC 13 on Jethro at that moment: he is frightened, not fanciful, and he goes outside and is sick by the corral. Nobody else hears it unless they are sitting with Lon.

CLUE C1 (core, automatic for Tabitha Lockhart if she is played; otherwise Lon carries it and it is on his body): the messenger's copy of the waybill, folded in an oilcloth wallet. 'Plata Vieja Consolidated Mining Co., June payroll: $3,600 in coin; $6,000 in currency, new issue, Bank of the Rio Abajo, per schedule attached.' The schedule is pinned to it in the cashier's neat hand: tens B 4401 to B 4700, fives A 2201 to A 2800. Most messengers never look at the schedule. Darius Crandall, the cashier, attaches one to every shipment because he was robbed in Kansas in 1874.

Celestino Trujillo, the People's candidate for probate judge, is carrying twelve hundred printed tickets and a letter from the community's lawyer in Albuquerque, Ezequiel Montaño, saying that the Company's suit will be heard on 18 July and that he must have the grant's act of possession, or a certified copy, before then. Celestino will show the letter to anyone who wins his trust, and will lecture anyone else about the grant.

Doroteo Griego at the Puerco station has accepted the Company's offer: he will keep the station for the Company when it buys it. He knows nothing of the robbery and is ashamed of the job. Persuasion DC 12: he admits it, and says a Company man came on Monday to count the horses.

keyLocations.name: The Puerto de Piedra
keyLocations.description: Nine miles east of the plaza, the road climbs a long grade through a gap in a basalt ridge. Black boulders the size of houses, junipers, a little dry arroyo on the south side of the road that runs back into the hills toward the Sierra Prieta. At the top of the grade the road bends between two outcrops and drops toward the plaza. A felled juniper lies across the road a hundred yards past the bend. The robbers' riflemen are in the rocks on the north outcrop, a hundred and fifty feet above the road, and Cade Rendell is on the ridge two hundred yards back with a buffalo rifle.
features: The top of the grade, where Jethro halts the team at a walk, a hundred yards before the felled tree, which he could not yet have seen from the bend
A strip of red flannel tied to a juniper on the north ridge, at the height of a man on a horse, visible from the box
The north outcrop: two firing positions behind stacked rocks, three-quarters cover, with .44 cartridge cases and an empty pasteboard cartridge box
The arroyo on the south side: soft sand, a juniper where five horses were tied, and the tracks going south
encounters: The robbery: Cade Rendell (Fast Gun) with a buffalo rifle on the ridge at 200 yards; Shad Sorrel (Bandit Sharpshooter) and Lige Tasker (Road Agent) on the north outcrop at 150 feet with three-quarters cover; Hob Linnet (Outlaw) and Rendell coming up out of the arroyo for the box once the coach is covered
Afterwards, the coach's six horses, one leader shot through the neck and screaming, and the passengers, one of them hysterical
secrets: CLUE F1 (core, automatic for anyone on the box or anyone who later asks Rafael Candelaria; Perception DC 12 for anyone inside): Jethro halted the team before the bend, a hundred yards short of the felled juniper, though from where he stopped the tree is hidden by the outcrop. A driver who halts for no reason at the top of a grade is either sick or knew. The red rag on the juniper is in plain sight of the box, and nobody but Jethro was looking for it.

CLUE A2 (core for anyone who speaks Spanish; Insight DC 12 for anyone else to notice that the voice is not local): the man on the rocks calling the orders in Spanish, '¡Manos arriba, todos abajo!', speaks the Spanish of the Texas border. He uses Texas words, says 'troca' for a wagon, and cannot roll his r's. Nicanor, Rafael, Patricio or Celestino know it at once: 'That's no vecino. That's a tejano gringo who learned it from his nurse.' The man who comes up out of the arroyo for the box gives his orders in English with a Texas drawl, and the passengers mostly remember the Spanish.

CLUE A3 (core for anyone who climbs to the north outcrop; Investigation DC 10 to find the box among the rocks): twenty-two .44 rimfire cases and an empty pasteboard cartridge box with a price stamp in purple ink: PARAGON MERCANTILE 75¢. The plaza's store sells cartridges loose from a keg, and never with a stamp.

Jethro throws down the padlock key when Rendell orders it. He has it off its thong before he is asked. Insight DC 14 for anyone watching him then: his hands are steady, and he does not look at the man with the gun. He looks at Lon.

Royal Penhallow, if he is played, knows the voice from the arroyo. It is Cade Rendell, who rode with him in Kansas in 1876 and was the one man of that gang who was never caught. Rendell knows Royal too, and says, quietly, as he goes back down with the box: 'Evening, Royal. Still shoeing horses for honest men?'

keyLocations.name: The arroyo and the trail south
keyLocations.description: The dry arroyo runs south from the gap for two miles, then climbs onto a mesa and into the foothills of the Sierra Prieta. The robbers' trail follows it: five horses, one pack animal for the box, heading south for the Cañoncito, eight miles away. A party that follows at once has two hours of light and then a moon two days past full.
features: The juniper where the horses were held: droppings, a cigarette end in brown paper, and a straw sombrero with a broken crown, dropped and trampled
Five sets of tracks: four shod horses and one unshod cow pony that left first, at a run, going west, not south
Where the trail climbs onto the mesa, a place where the gang stopped and someone lashed the box to the pack horse
A cow pony's tracks going west across the llano toward the Ojo del Gato, alone, and quickly
encounters: A rattlesnake in the rocks where the horses were held (Rattlesnake), for whoever reaches under the juniper for the sombrero
If the party follows the trail after dark: Lige Tasker (Road Agent) left behind on the mesa rim to discourage pursuit, with a rifle and a good view
secrets: CLUE A1 (core for a Blacksmith, a Scout's Trailcraft or a Cowhand; Survival DC 13 otherwise): the four shod horses wear factory-made shoes, machine-pressed with a crease and stamped nail holes, of the kind the Paragon Livery buys by the keg from St. Louis. Every smith on the plaza forges his own shoes by hand and every vecino's horse wears them, heavier and uneven. The fifth horse is an unshod cow pony, which is what a vaquero of the commons rides.

CLUE A5 (the start of it): the sombrero is a cheap plaza straw with a horsehair band. Burned inside the band with a hot wire are the letters T.A. Nicanor knows it at once. It is his brother Tiburcio's. Rafael and Celestino know it too, and Celestino goes grey and says nothing. If the party leaves the sombrero, Rendell, who comes back at dusk to make sure of it, puts it on the road where the Paragon men will find it on Friday.

The cow pony's tracks go west toward the Ojo del Gato and Rufina Sedillo's sheep camp. A party with a Scout or a Cowhand can follow them there by midnight. If they do, they find Tiburcio, and the fear on him, a day before the Committee knows where to look (see st-scenario-002).

Following the shod horses south leads to the Cañoncito by full dark. Rendell, Sorrel and Tasker are there. Hob Linnet leaves at dawn on Friday by the old sheep trail north to Paragon, with the $6,000 in notes in his saddlebags. A party that cuts across the mesa before dawn can catch him alone (Survival DC 15 to guess the route; Trailcraft finds it).

keyLocations.name: Santa Teresita: the home station and the plaza
keyLocations.description: The coach comes into the plaza at about seven on Thursday evening, at a walk, with a dead man on the roof. The church bell rings for him. The home station is on the east side of the plaza: corrals, a smithy, the station house and Doña Eufemia Ludlow's eating house under a long portal. On Friday morning the justice of the peace, Anacleto Lovato, holds the inquest in the courthouse's long room. Sheriff Florencio Jaramillo has two deputies, a jail of two cells and a strong dislike of Paragon.
features: Doña Eufemia's portal, where Lon is laid on a door between two trestles and the station women wash him
The smithy, where Royal Penhallow works, with hand-forged shoes hanging on pegs by size
The courthouse's long room, with benches, a crucifix, a territorial flag and a table for the justice
Jethro Petree's little house behind the corrals, where his wife, Doña Luz, keeps hens
encounters: No set combat. On the plaza on Thursday night a crowd of young men want to ride out after the robbers and are not going to wait for anyone
Cyprian Ludlow, who wants to drive the coach on to Plata Vieja on Friday with the mail and no money, out of pride
secrets: CLUE A4 (core for a Doc, or automatic at the inquest if anyone asks the doctor; Medicine DC 12 otherwise): Lon Brisbane was killed by a single heavy ball, .50 calibre, through the chest from in front and above, from at least 150 yards. It went through him and through the seat back. Only a buffalo rifle throws a ball like that. No vecino owns one. Sheriff Jaramillo knows of one rifle like it in the county: a Texan in Paragon, a week ago, at the Silver Rail.

CLUE C4 and F2 (Investigation DC 13 to search Jethro's coat or his house; or Persuasion DC 14 with Doña Luz once she trusts the party): five new twenty-dollar gold coins, double eagles dated 1880, wrapped in a bandanna at the bottom of his trunk. No driver on the line has been paid in gold in two years, because Ludlow pays in silver when he pays at all. On Saturday Doña Luz spends one at the plaza store for flour and coffee, and the storekeeper, who has never had change for a double eagle, tells the whole plaza.

Jethro lies at the inquest. He says the robbers had the tree across the road and he stopped for it. Rafael Candelaria, who was on the roof, starts to say that they stopped before the bend, then looks at the old man and doesn't. Insight DC 12: Rafael is protecting Jethro, and knows he is.

At the inquest Ollie Gruber and two passengers swear that the robbers spoke Spanish. The justice records 'Mexican bandits, persons unknown'. A party that puts A1 to A4 in front of him can have the record read 'persons unknown, not of this county' instead. That costs the Company its story in the plaza, but not in Paragon.

keyLocations.name: Paragon: the Silver Rail, the Paragon House and the livery
keyLocations.description: Eighteen miles north across the llano. Coldiron Avenue is wide and new, with plank sidewalks, painted false fronts, a brass band that practises on the depot platform in the evenings, and the water tank like a monument. The Paragon House has a register and a clerk who reads it. The Silver Rail has a mahogany bar brought from Kansas City and a faro table. The Paragon Livery & Feed has a smith, an Englishman named Hosea Durrant, and a book. Behind the depot is the Laguna section gang's bunkhouse and Victoriano Romero's section house.
features: The Paragon Pioneer's window, where on Friday a poster goes up: $1,000 REWARD, THE SANTA TERESITA BANDITS, with Tiburcio Archibeque's name and description
The Paragon House register on the clerk's counter, open for anyone to sign and to read
The livery's hire book and its keg of factory shoes from St. Louis
The depot telegraph office, where the operator, a Company man named Uriah Quist, reads every wire
encounters: Constable Ott Ebner (Crooked Sheriff) and four Committee men (Deputy), who don't like strangers asking about the hotel register
A drunk railroad man (Drunk Cowboy) at the Silver Rail who wants to fight the first Mexican he sees, and is stopped, quietly and firmly, by Victoriano Romero's section gang
secrets: CLUE B1 (Investigation DC 12 to read the register without the clerk seeing; or Persuasion DC 13, or a $5 note, to have him show it): 'C. Rendell and three, Texas. 22 June to 27 June. Rooms 4 and 5. Charge to P.T.&I. Co. — F.R.' The clerk remembers them: a tall fair man with a buffalo rifle in a case, a dark one who spoke Spanish to the cook, a red-haired boy and a heavy man called Hob.

CLUE B2 (Persuasion DC 12 with Hosea Durrant, who is honest and doesn't know what the hire was for; Intimidation DC 14 works too but costs Reputation in Paragon): the hire book shows four saddle horses hired on 27 June 'for a fortnight, horse buying, L. Tasker, on the Company's account'. A bay gelding came back lame on the night of 1 July, ridden hard, with a man who paid the hire in cash and went to the Paragon House. Durrant shod all four himself, with the factory shoes from the keg.

CLUE B4 (Victoriano Romero tells it only to someone who treats him as a foreman, not a curiosity, and who asks him straight; Persuasion DC 13): he saw the four ride out south at dawn on 27 June, with the red-haired one leading, and on the night of 1 July saw the heavy one ride back in on a lame bay with saddlebags so heavy that he lifted them down with both hands. 'He went to the hotel. Then a man from the hotel took the saddlebags to the store, by the back.' He has his own reasons to watch the Company, which are Laguna's, and he does not explain them yet (see st-scenario-002).

Fenton Rusk is at the Silver Rail on Friday night, buying drinks for the Committee, and is charming to strangers. If the party says anything about serial numbers in Paragon, he hears it by morning. If they wire Albuquerque for the schedule from the Paragon depot, Uriah Quist copies the wire to Rusk within the hour, and Rusk begins changing notes for old ones at the Mercantile's safe.

synopsis: The last run of the Rio Seco Mail & Stage Line, and the robbery that is meant to decide an election. On Wednesday 29 June coach No. 7 leaves Albuquerque with the Plata Vieja payroll, the mail, Celestino Trujillo, a drummer and the party. That night at the Puerco station, old Jethro Petree tries to keep Lon Brisbane off the box and can't say why. On Thursday afternoon at the Puerto de Piedra Jethro halts at a red rag, Cade Rendell shoots Lon dead from two hundred yards, and four men take the box. One of them gives his orders in Spanish. The party can fight, and should be allowed to win something: a wounded robber, a dead one, a saved horse, a passenger kept alive. The box goes down the arroyo regardless, unless they do something extraordinary. In the arroyo they find a boy's sombrero, factory horseshoes and a Paragon cartridge box. They can follow the robbers south toward the Cañoncito, follow the boy west toward the Ojo del Gato, or bring the dead man home. In Santa Teresita the bell rings. On Friday the inquest records Mexican bandits, the Company's buckboard carries the first mail, and by Friday night the Paragon Citizens' Committee has posted $1,000 for Tiburcio Archibeque. On Saturday Constable Ebner and twelve Paragon men ride to the plaza to take the boy, and Sheriff Jaramillo meets them in the plaza with two deputies and the whole of Santa Teresita behind him. That evening the wire at Paragon says the President has been shot. By Lon's funeral on Sunday the party should know three things: the robbers came from Paragon, the old driver knew, and someone wrote down the numbers on the notes.
hook: Wednesday, six in the morning, Albuquerque: the coach, the box, the notice on the door. The party are passengers, or are riding with the coach. Cyprian Ludlow shakes each of their hands. 'Thirteen years and never lost a sack,' he says. 'I'd take it kindly if you'd help me keep it that way to the end. I'll stand you all a dinner at my wife's table in Santa Teresita.' On the box, Jethro Petree raises his whip to the old man, and doesn't quite smile.

conclusions.conclusion: A. The robbers were not Santa Teresita men
clues: A1: factory shoes on four horses, an unshod cow pony (the arroyo)
A2: the Spanish was a tejano's; the leader was a Texan (the Puerto de Piedra)
A3: .44 cases and a Paragon Mercantile cartridge box (the north outcrop)
A4: a .50 buffalo-rifle ball from 200 yards (the inquest, the doctor)
A5: the sombrero is Tiburcio's, and the cow pony ran west alone (the arroyo)

conclusions.conclusion: B. The robbers came out of Paragon
clues: B1: 'C. Rendell and three', charged to the Company (the Paragon House)
B2: four horses hired by L. Tasker, one back lame on 1 July (the livery)
B4: Victoriano Romero saw them leave and saw the saddlebags go to the store (the section house)
B5: the broken box at the Cañoncito, if the party follows the robbers there
F1: he halted before the bend, at the red rag (the Puerto de Piedra, Rafael)
F2 and C4: five new double eagles in his trunk (his house, Doña Luz, the plaza store)
His request that Lon ride inside, and the padlock key ready in his hand (the Puerco station, the robbery)

acts.title: Wednesday and Thursday: The Last Run Out
acts.description: The road out and the robbery. Spend the first hour letting the players meet each other and the people on the coach. Make Jethro and Lon likeable, because one is going to die and the other is going to be the reason. Then the Puerto de Piedra. The robbery is meant to succeed. Lon's death is the opening of the fight, not something the party can prevent, so run it as read-aloud. Everything after that first shot is the players' to change.
objectives: Meet the coach, its people and the road, and learn what the payroll is
Notice what is wrong with Jethro Petree at the Puerco station
Survive the robbery and keep the passengers alive
Take something from the robbers: a man, a horse, a face, a voice, a direction

scenes.name: La Doña
scenes.description: The road west out of Albuquerque: across the river, through Atrisco, up the Ceja and out onto the llano, with team changes every twelve miles. Introduce Jethro on the box, singing to the horses; Lon Brisbane, big, freckled and kind, who has a Sunday-school text for every situation and a sawed-off shotgun; Rafael Candelaria on the roof, twenty-two and in love with everything; Celestino Trujillo inside, eloquent and a little pompous, explaining the grant to anyone who will listen; and Ollie Gruber, the drummer, who sells whiskey and cheats at cards. This is the scene for the players to introduce their characters to one another. Celestino will talk politics, which is a way of telling the players what the campaign is about.
scenes.readAloud: The coach goes down to the river at a trot, and the town falls away behind you: adobe and new brick, the church towers in the old plaza, the depot smoke in the new town, a train whistle that sounds like the future. Then the bridge, and the cottonwoods of Atrisco, and the long climb up the Ceja with the six horses leaning into their collars and Jethro Petree singing to them in Spanish and English, a hymn and a love song and something rude about a mule. At the top the whole of the west opens out, a hundred miles of pale grass and black mesa under a white-hot sky, with blue mountains at the edge of the world. Inside the coach it is already a hundred degrees. A well-dressed Hispano man in a black coat leans forward, sets a carpet bag on his knees and says, 'You are going to Santa Teresita? Then you should know what you are riding into. There is going to be an election.'

skillChecks.success: You read the people on the coach. Celestino is proud, sincere and afraid of losing. Gruber is harmless and a cheat. Lon is exactly what he looks like. Jethro is somewhere else. He hasn't looked back at the box once, and drivers always do.
skillChecks.failure: Hot, crowded and friendly. A long day ahead.

skillChecks.success: Gruber's deck is shaved at the corners and his left sleeve is too full. You can win his money back from him or shame him, and the coach laughs either way. Lon says, 'Proverbs, chapter eleven: a false balance is abomination,' and confiscates the deck.
skillChecks.failure: You lose $3 to Gruber before somebody notices how.

skillChecks.success: Celestino shows you Licenciado Montaño's letter: the Company's suit comes before the court on 18 July, and the grant must answer with its act of possession or lose the commons by default. 'The Company has our patrón, Don Fermín. It wants the courthouse. And now it has the mail. What will it want next, our church?'
skillChecks.failure: Celestino lectures you on the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo for an hour. You learn that he is running for probate judge and that he thinks you should vote for him.

scenes.name: The Puerco Station
scenes.description: Night at the Puerco crossing: the dry sand river, the adobe station, the ramada, a fiddle, mutton stew and the keeper's wife's tortillas. It is the line's last night here, and everyone knows it. Ludlow's keeper, Doroteo Griego, is going to work for the Company and is ashamed of it. After supper Jethro asks Lon, twice, to ride inside tomorrow. Lon laughs it off. Jethro goes out to the corral and is sick. If a player sits with Lon, Lon tells them about his partner, Tabitha, if she isn't played, or about his mother in Topeka, and recites the Twenty-third Psalm at the stars because it is what he does on the road.
scenes.readAloud: The station is a low adobe square with a brush ramada along the front and a well with a wooden sweep. The sand bed of the Rio Puerco is a quarter of a mile wide and dry as a road, with a trickle down the middle you could step over. 'Two hours after a rain,' the keeper says, 'you could drown a coach in it.' There is mutton and chile and coffee, and a boy plays the fiddle under the ramada. The drivers and the keeper talk in low voices about thirteen years and who will have work next month. Lon Brisbane sits on an upturned bucket and oils his shotgun, and when the old driver comes over and says something to him in a low voice, Lon throws back his head and laughs. 'Ride inside? Jethro, I'd as soon ride in the mail sack.' The old man laughs too. Then he walks out into the dark toward the corral and doesn't come back for a long time.

skillChecks.success: Jethro wasn't joking. He asked Lon twice, and when Lon refused the second time his face went the colour of ashes. Out at the corral you hear him being sick. When he comes back he is cheerful and loud and drinks another cup of the keeper's mescal.
skillChecks.failure: An old man's joke between friends. The fiddle plays on.

skillChecks.success: If you go to Jethro at the corral and are kind, he very nearly tells you. 'Something I done, I can't undo. Don't you ride on top tomorrow, that's all.' Then he hears himself and says it's the mescal talking. He will remember that you were kind. In st-scenario-002 he will come to you first.
skillChecks.failure: Jethro tells you to mind your own business, not unkindly, and goes to sleep in the coach.

skillChecks.success: In the night a rider comes up to the station from the west, waters a horse at the well without coming in, and leaves again westward. In the morning the keeper says it was nobody, a sheepherder. In the moonlight you saw a Texas saddle and a rifle case long enough for a buffalo gun.
skillChecks.failure: You sleep like the dead. The coyotes sing all night.

scenes.name: The Puerto de Piedra
scenes.description: Thursday, about twenty to four in the afternoon, nine miles from the plaza. The robbery, run in three beats. First the halt and the shot, which is read-aloud: Lon dies. Then the stand-off: two riflemen on the rocks at 150 feet with three-quarters cover, a man calling orders in Spanish, and a leader horse shot in the traces so that the coach cannot run. Then Rendell and Linnet come up the arroyo for the box, and Jethro throws the key down. The players can fight from the coach (soft cover), from under it, or from the boulders on the south side. Sorrel and Tasker shoot to pin, not to kill, unless someone hurts them. Rendell, back on the ridge with his buffalo rifle, takes one more shot at anyone who stands on the box with a gun. If the party kills or drops one robber, the rest still go. If they do something extraordinary, such as holding the boot, killing two, or shooting the pack horse, the box may stay. Let it, and see the twists. The gang is gone down the arroyo within five rounds.
scenes.readAloud: The grade is long and the horses are blowing, and Jethro lets them walk. The road climbs between black boulders and twisted junipers into a notch in the ridge, and the air is still and very hot, and somewhere a canyon wren is singing its falling song. At the top, just short of the bend, Jethro draws the team up. He looks up at the ridge on the right, where a strip of red cloth hangs from a juniper. 'Breather,' he says. Lon Brisbane half turns on the box to say something to him. The sound comes a long moment after: a single flat heavy crack that rolls back and forth between the rocks. Lon sits down very slowly, as if someone had asked him to, and the shotgun slides off his knees into the road. Then the rocks above you are shouting. '¡Manos arriba! ¡Todos abajo! ¡Abajo, abajo!' A rifle barks, and the near leader screams and goes down in the traces, and the coach jolts and stops dead.

skillChecks.success: Two riflemen in the rocks to the north, one dark, one red-haired, both masked with bandannas. Somewhere far back on the ridge is the big rifle that killed Lon; you saw the smoke. Two more men are coming up the arroyo on the south side, on foot, leading a pack horse. You can see them, and they don't yet know it.
skillChecks.failure: Rocks, smoke, shouting in two languages, a dead man on the box. You can't tell how many or where.

skillChecks.success: You cut the screaming leader out of the traces, or calm the other five enough that the coach can move. If someone takes the lines, the coach can be driven on with four or five horses. Running the grade under fire is a chase (combat.json chases) with the robbers on foot, and the riflemen get one volley at it.
skillChecks.failure: The team is plunging and tangled. The coach isn't going anywhere until the shooting stops.

skillChecks.success: You shout back, in whichever language you choose, and something in it makes the man coming up for the box hesitate. Rendell calls him on, but the hesitation is a free round for anyone with a gun. If Royal Penhallow is played, he can use Rendell's name; the tall man stops dead for a heartbeat and then laughs.
skillChecks.failure: Nobody on the rocks cares what you say. A bullet takes the lamp off the coach six inches from your head.

encounters: The robbery: Cade Rendell (Fast Gun), buffalo rifle at 200 yards, one shot a round at most and only at someone on the box; Shad Sorrel (Bandit Sharpshooter) and Lige Tasker (Road Agent) on the north outcrop, 150 ft, three-quarters cover; Hob Linnet (Outlaw) and then Rendell coming up the arroyo for the box. The coach's sides are soft cover; the boulders on the south side are full cover. The gang withdraws by round five
Ollie Gruber, the drummer, panics and tries to run. A rifleman will shoot him unless someone stops him

acts.title: Thursday Night: The Dead Man on the Box
acts.description: After the robbery the party has to choose, and the choice matters. They can follow the robbers south, follow the cow pony west, or take the coach and the dead man home. A party can split, which is dramatic and dangerous. Whatever they choose, Rafael Candelaria will drive the coach on if nobody else can. Celestino will go with it, because the plaza must hear the news from him. The evidence in the arroyo is the scenario's core. Let the players look as long as they like, and let the light go while they do.
objectives: Read the arroyo: the shoes, the sombrero, the cartridges, the rag
Decide whether to pursue, and whom
Bring Lon Brisbane home, and tell the plaza what happened before rumour does
Keep the plaza's young men from riding out blind after 'the bandits'

scenes.name: The Arroyo
scenes.description: Five horses were tied to a juniper in the arroyo below the road. Here are the factory shoes, the trampled sombrero with T.A. burned in the band, the cigarette end, and the cow pony that bolted west alone. Up on the north outcrop are the cartridges and the Paragon cartridge box, and on the ridge the red rag and the place where a man lay with a long rifle. This is the scene where the case is born. If Nicanor is played, the sombrero is the moment his campaign begins. Put it in his hands and let him decide what to do with it.
scenes.readAloud: The arroyo is a dry sandy wash with juniper on the banks, and in the shade of the biggest tree the sand is churned and fouled where horses stood a long time, stamping at the flies. Brown cigarette paper. A place where someone sat with his back to the trunk. Half trodden into the sand is a straw sombrero with a broken crown and a horsehair band, the kind every boy on the plaza wears to work. Five sets of tracks leave the tree. Four go south down the wash at a steady trot, deep, the horses carrying weight, and one of them leading a pack animal. The fifth, small and unshod, goes up the west bank in great scrambling leaps and away across the llano toward the mountains, alone, as fast as a pony can run.

skillChecks.success: The four shod horses wear factory shoes: thin, machine-pressed, with a crease round the toe and square-punched nail holes. A vecino's horse wears hand-forged iron. These horses were shod in a town with a railroad (CLUE A1; automatic for a Blacksmith, a Scout's Trailcraft or a Cowhand). The cow pony was ridden by someone light, and in terror.
skillChecks.failure: Horses, a lot of them, going south. And one going west in a hurry.

skillChecks.success: Inside the sombrero's band, burned with a hot wire: T.A. Up on the north outcrop, twenty-two .44 rimfire cases and an empty cartridge box stamped PARAGON MERCANTILE 75¢ (CLUE A3). On the ridge two hundred yards back, the flattened grass where a man lay to shoot, a single big .50 case he didn't bother to pick up, and the red rag tied at the height of a mounted man where a driver on the box would see it.
skillChecks.failure: You find the sombrero, and nothing else that means anything yet.

skillChecks.success: Whoever is holding the sombrero, Nicanor or Celestino or Rafael, knows whose it is and is trying not to show it. If you ask gently they tell you: Tiburcio Archibeque, seventeen, a vaquero of the commons, and the best rider on the plaza. 'He's a child. He wouldn't. He couldn't.' And then, very quietly: 'Then why did he run?'
skillChecks.failure: Somebody's hat. Every boy in the county wears one like it.

scenes.name: Santa Teresita at Dark
scenes.description: The coach comes into the plaza at a walk at about seven, with Lon on the roof under a slicker and the church bell ringing. Doña Eufemia Ludlow takes charge of the dead and the living. Cyprian Ludlow takes it badly: thirteen years, and his last run is a dead man and a lost box. Sheriff Jaramillo arrives at a run with two deputies. On the plaza a crowd forms, and thirty young men want to ride out after 'the bandits' tonight, which in the dark means shooting at any rider on the commons. Zadok Morgenstern, if played, or the plaza's curandera, Doña Paz Montoya, if not, examines the body.
scenes.readAloud: The plaza is a square of low adobe walls gone rose and gold in the last light, with a single huge cottonwood in the middle and the church's two white towers at the end. The bell starts as the coach comes round the corner, slow and single, and people come out of every door. Women in black rebozos, men in shirtsleeves, children, dogs. A tall old woman in black silk comes down the portal steps of the station house as the coach stops, looks up at the shape on the roof, and crosses herself. Then she says, in a voice that carries across the whole plaza, 'Bring him down to me. Gently. Gently, I said.' Behind her a white-bearded man in a linen coat stands with his hand on the coach wheel and doesn't move at all.

skillChecks.success: One heavy ball through the chest from in front and above, from a long way off. It went through him and through the seat back. A .50 calibre buffalo rifle, at a hundred and fifty yards or more (CLUE A4; automatic for a Doc's Diagnosis). Sheriff Jaramillo, listening, says there's one rifle like that in the county he knows of, a Texan's, seen at the Silver Rail in Paragon a week ago.
skillChecks.failure: He was shot once and died at once. That much is plain to anyone.

skillChecks.success: You stop the young men riding out tonight, with evidence (the factory shoes, the Paragon cartridge box), with Celestino's help, or with plain sense: in the dark they'll kill a sheepherder. Reputation in Santa Teresita +1. The sheriff remembers it.
skillChecks.failure: A dozen young men ride out with torches. They find nothing and shoot a Laguna section hand's mule on the Paragon road by mistake, which Victoriano Romero will mention to you in st-scenario-002.

skillChecks.success: Jethro Petree tells the sheriff the robbers had the tree across the road. Rafael Candelaria starts to say 'No, we stopped before…' and then looks at Jethro and stops. Rafael knows something about the old man and loves him too much to say it.
skillChecks.failure: Everybody tells the sheriff the same story: Mexican bandits, four or five, a tree across the road.

scenes.name: The Cañoncito
scenes.description: For a party that follows the robbers south. Eight miles down the arroyo, across a mesa and into a box canyon in the foothills: an abandoned sheep camp, a stone corral, a roofless jacal and a seep spring. Rendell, Sorrel and Tasker are here until Monday. Linnet leaves at dawn on Friday with the notes by the old sheep trail north. A party that arrives by night faces three good gunmen in a stone corral with a single way in. A frontal attack is a hard fight for this level, and Rendell will leave if it goes against him. A party that watches instead can see Linnet ride out at dawn and catch him alone on the trail, which is the scenario's best prize.
scenes.readAloud: The canyon opens out of the mesa's rim like a door in a wall: red rock on three sides, a fringe of juniper, and at the head of it a spring that makes a patch of green no bigger than a room. Beside the spring is an old sheep camp, a stone corral chest-high and a jacal of juniper poles with no roof. There is a small fire, carefully hidden in the angle of the corral wall, and you can smell coffee and horses. Someone laughs, and someone else says, in English with a Texas drawl, 'Keep your voice down, Hob. You'll wake the dead.' And somebody else laughs at that, too.

skillChecks.success: You get close enough to see and hear. Four men, five horses, the broken box by the fire (CLUE B5). The coin is in two canvas sacks; the notes are in the heavy man's saddlebags, and the tall fair one is telling him to 'take these to the gentleman at the hotel, by the back, and don't stop for a drink.' He leaves at first light.
skillChecks.failure: A horse in the corral whickers at yours. The fire goes out. Somewhere in the rocks a rifle lever works, very quietly.

skillChecks.success: You find the old sheep trail north over the mesa, the way a rider would go to Paragon without using the road, and a place on it two miles out where one man could be stopped by two (automatic with Trailcraft). Hob Linnet rides into you at seven on Friday morning with $6,000 in his saddlebags.
skillChecks.failure: You can't find the trail he'll take. He goes by you a mile off at dawn, and you see the dust too late.

skillChecks.success: If you take Hob Linnet alive, he is heavy, slow and frightened of Rendell, and he talks: Rendell's name, Sorrel's and Tasker's, and 'the gentleman at the hotel' who hired them, though he never heard his name. He'll say it again before a judge if he believes you can keep him alive (CLUE B6, partial C6).
skillChecks.failure: Linnet says nothing at all, and you can see he is more afraid of the man back in the canyon than of you.

encounters: The Cañoncito: Cade Rendell (Fast Gun), Shad Sorrel (Bandit Sharpshooter) and Lige Tasker (Road Agent) in the stone corral (half cover, full cover behind the jacal's stone base), with a single approach up the canyon floor. Rendell leaves at the first sign he is losing
Hob Linnet (Outlaw) alone on the sheep trail at dawn on Friday, with the notes

acts.title: Friday to Sunday: A Poster with a Boy's Name
acts.description: The Company makes its move and the party sees its shape. Friday is the inquest in the morning and Paragon at night. Saturday is the Committee's riders at the plaza and the news from Washington. Sunday is the funeral. The party can be in only some of these places, which is the point. A party that goes to Paragon on Friday can read the register and the livery book and see the poster go up. A party that stays on the plaza meets Ebner's riders on Saturday.
objectives: Get the inquest to record the truth, or as much of it as the party can prove
Go to Paragon and find where the robbers stayed and whose horses they rode
Keep Ebner's riders from taking Tiburcio, or anyone else, out of the plaza
Decide what to do about Jethro Petree

scenes.name: The Inquest
scenes.description: Friday at nine in the courthouse's long room, before Justice Anacleto Lovato, a cautious old man who writes very slowly. Witnesses: Jethro, Rafael, the passengers, the party, and Doña Paz or Zadok for the body. Jethro lies about the tree. The drummer swears the bandits were Mexicans. The justice will record whatever the evidence in front of him supports, and no more. A party that puts the shoes, the cartridge box and the rifle ball before him gets 'persons unknown, not of this county'. That is the first time anyone official has said it, and the plaza hears it.
scenes.readAloud: The long room smells of whitewash and old grain, from the days when it was the Lucero storehouse. Benches, a crucifix on the end wall, a territorial flag on a pole, a pine table with a ledger and an inkpot, and behind it a small old man in a black coat who dips his pen, writes a word, and blots it before he writes the next. Lon Brisbane lies on a door on two trestles under a clean sheet. The room is full. At the back, by the door, stands a man nobody on the plaza knows: dark suit, gold watch-chain, a straw boater in his hand, a pleasant attentive face. When the drummer says 'Mexicans, I'd swear to it,' the man by the door smiles, and writes something in a little book.

skillChecks.success: With at least two of A1 to A4 in front of him, Justice Lovato writes 'by persons unknown, not of this county, as the evidence of the horseshoes and the ball shows'. Reputation in Santa Teresita +1, and the People's party's attitude improves by one step. The man at the back closes his notebook and leaves before the end.
skillChecks.failure: The record reads 'Mexican bandits, persons unknown'. By the evening it is in the Paragon Pioneer, and by Saturday it is on the poster.

skillChecks.success: Jethro's story about the tree is a lie, and Rafael knows it. The man at the back is Fenton Rusk, the Company's election agent, though nobody here can name him yet. He came to hear what the plaza knows.
skillChecks.failure: The old driver tells it well, and everyone believes him.

skillChecks.success: If you press Jethro in front of the room, he breaks down and says only: 'I couldn't see the tree. I couldn't. I stopped. God forgive me, I stopped.' The justice writes it down. It is not a confession, but it is a crack, and everyone in the room heard it, including the man at the back. Jethro is in danger from this moment on.
skillChecks.failure: Jethro looks at you with such misery that the room turns against you, not him. Reputation in Santa Teresita -1.

scenes.name: The Committee
scenes.description: Friday night in Paragon. The band plays on the depot platform. The Paragon Citizens' Committee meets in the Silver Rail's back room: Constable Ebner, the Pioneer's editor, three merchants, Fenton Rusk buying the drinks, and Everard Coldiron, who speaks for two minutes about law and order and the future of the county and leaves. At ten the poster goes up in the Pioneer's window: $1,000 REWARD, THE SANTA TERESITA BANDITS, with Tiburcio Archibeque's name and a description. A party in Paragon can read the hotel register (B1), the livery book (B2), and talk to Victoriano Romero behind the depot (B4). They should be careful: Paragon does not like questions from people who came in on the plaza's coach.
scenes.readAloud: Paragon at night is all lamplight and new paint. The false fronts along Coldiron Avenue are white and blue and red, the plank sidewalks still smell of the sawmill, and a brass band in borrowed uniforms is playing 'Garryowen' on the depot platform under the water tank for a crowd of railroad men, cowboys, a few women and a great many dogs. The Silver Rail's doors are open and its piano is going. In the window of the Paragon Pioneer, a man in shirtsleeves is pasting up a poster with the ink still wet on it: $1,000 REWARD. THE SANTA TERESITA BANDITS. For information leading to the arrest of TIBURCIO ARCHIBEQUE, a Mexican, about 17 years, slight, who rides a paint pony, and his confederates. Below that, smaller: By order of the Paragon Citizens' Committee. LAW, ORDER AND PROGRESS.

skillChecks.success: The Paragon House register: 'C. Rendell and three, Texas. 22 June to 27 June. Rooms 4 and 5. Charge to P.T.&I. Co. — F.R.' (CLUE B1). The clerk, asked, says F.R. is Mr. Rusk, who handles the Company's election business and has room 2.
skillChecks.failure: The clerk closes the register and asks, loudly, whether you're with the plaza crowd. Two Committee men at the bar turn round to look.

skillChecks.success: Hosea Durrant at the livery shows you the hire book: four horses hired on 27 June by L. Tasker on the Company's account, one bay back lame on the night of the 1st. He shod all four himself with the factory shoes from the keg (CLUE B2). He's an honest man and he goes pale as he works it out. 'I'll say it to a judge,' he says. 'Not to Ebner.'
skillChecks.failure: Durrant won't talk in front of his boy and the constable's horse at the rail. Come back when it's quiet.

skillChecks.success: At the Silver Rail, Rusk is the most interesting man in the room: easy, generous, laughing, the one everybody is watching even while Coldiron talks. He is the only man in Paragon who looks at the poster as if he had written it. If you speak to him, he is delighted to meet you and asks a great many questions about what you saw.
skillChecks.failure: A town in a good mood, a poster, a band. The Company's manager makes a fine short speech.

scenes.name: Saturday: Twelve Riders at the Plaza
scenes.description: Saturday about noon, Constable Ott Ebner and twelve Committee men ride into Santa Teresita with the poster and a warrant from a Paragon justice of the peace, to arrest Tiburcio and search the Archibeque house. Sheriff Jaramillo meets them in the plaza with two deputies and says that Paragon's warrants don't run in the county seat without his say. Behind him the plaza fills. It can go very badly. Ebner's men are not killers, except two of them, and the vecinos are not armed, except about sixty. The party can stand with the sheriff, talk Ebner down, shame him, or show him that his own Committee's evidence points to Paragon. That evening the wire at Paragon brings news that the President has been shot at a railroad station in Washington. Both towns go quiet for a night. Sunday is Lon Brisbane's funeral at the church, with Tabitha or Ludlow speaking for him.
scenes.readAloud: They come across the llano in a long line of dust: a dozen riders, rifles across their saddles, a buckboard behind with the Paragon Pioneer's editor in it. The man in front wears a nickel-plated star and a new hat. They rein in by the cottonwood in the middle of the plaza, and the doors and shutters round the square open one by one. Out of the courthouse comes Sheriff Florencio Jaramillo, a heavy grey man in his shirtsleeves, without a hat, with a shotgun in the crook of his arm and two young deputies behind him. He stops in the sun ten paces from the constable's horse. 'Good afternoon, Ebner,' he says in English. 'This is the county seat. If you have paper for me I will read it. If you came to take somebody's child, you will have to go through me, and then through them.' He doesn't look round. He doesn't need to.

skillChecks.success: You talk Ebner down: his warrant was sworn by a Paragon justice with no jurisdiction here, his evidence is a hat, and the robbers' horses came out of his own town's livery. He doesn't believe the last part, but he believes the rest, and his men are looking at the doors. He rides home. Reputation in Santa Teresita +2. The Committee's attitude hardens.
skillChecks.failure: Ebner won't go without something. He arrests Celestino Trujillo, the boy's uncle, for 'harbouring', and the plaza explodes. Unless the party stops it, a stone is thrown, a gun goes off and a Committee man is hit.

skillChecks.success: You stand beside the sheriff, armed, and the constable counts you and does the arithmetic. He leaves, promising to come back with more men. Reputation in Santa Teresita +1, in Paragon -1.
skillChecks.failure: One of Ebner's two hard men, a Hired Gun named Pratt, calls you out. It is a showdown (frontier.json), here, now, in the plaza, unless someone stops it.

skillChecks.success: At Lon Brisbane's funeral on Sunday you speak for him, or help Tabitha or Cyprian Ludlow to. The whole plaza is there, and so is Victoriano Romero's section gang, who have walked eighteen miles because Lon once carried a sick Laguna boy to the doctor on the box. Both towns' anger goes quiet for an hour. Reputation in Santa Teresita +1.
skillChecks.failure: The funeral is decent and short. Afterwards, everyone goes home angry.

encounters: No set combat at the inquest or the Committee. In Paragon, Constable Ebner (Crooked Sheriff) and four Committee men (Deputy) start trouble with strangers who ask about the register

Saturday on the plaza: Constable Ebner (Crooked Sheriff), two hard men (Hired Gun) and ten Committee riders (Deputy or Vigilante) against Sheriff Jaramillo (use Deputy, with Lawman features), his two deputies (Deputy) and an angry plaza. It should not become a fight, and it can

npcsInvolved.name: Jethro Petree, 61
npcsInvolved.role: The line's oldest driver; the inside man
npcsInvolved.description: Small, bandy, white-whiskered, with a face like a dried apple and big gentle hands that can hold six horses on a grade. He has driven this road since 1868 and sings to the horses in two languages. He has a wife, Doña Luz, a little house behind the corrals and no money at all. He was promised a job and $500 in gold and told nobody would be hurt.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To have work when he is too old for the box, and now to undo something he cannot undo. Every hour Lon is dead he is a little less able to bear it.

npcsInvolved.name: Lon Brisbane, 29
npcsInvolved.role: Southwestern Express messenger; dies at the Puerto de Piedra
npcsInvolved.description: Big, freckled, red-haired, from Topeka, a Sunday-school teacher's son with a Bible verse for everything and a sawed-off shotgun across his knees. Tabitha Lockhart's partner on the Rio Seco run for two years. Liked by everyone on the road.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To bring the box in and go home to Kansas in the autumn. He dies in the first second of the scenario. Make the players miss him.

npcsInvolved.name: Cyprian Ludlow, 66
npcsInvolved.role: Owner of the Rio Seco Mail & Stage Line
npcsInvolved.description: A tall white-bearded Vermonter who came out with the army in 1862, married Eufemia Gallardo of Santa Teresita in 1866, and started the line in 1868 with one coach and a mail contract. Proud, stubborn and courteous. He owes the Bank of the Rio Abajo $4,000, and has never lost a mail sack.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To end his line with its name clean. After the robbery, to find who did it, and not to sell la Doña to anyone.

npcsInvolved.name: Doña Eufemia Gallardo de Ludlow, 58
npcsInvolved.role: Cyprian's wife; runs the home station and the eating house
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, severe, in black silk, born on the plaza, with the best kitchen in the county and the sharpest tongue. She runs the station, the women and, when he lets her, her husband.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To bury Lon properly, feed the living and see her husband's name kept. She is the plaza's opinion of the party.

npcsInvolved.name: Celestino Trujillo, 34
npcsInvolved.role: Schoolmaster; the People's candidate for probate judge; Tiburcio's uncle
npcsInvolved.description: Slim, handsome, black-coated, with a scholar's spectacles and an orator's voice, educated by the Jesuits at Las Vegas. Proud, sincere and a little vain. He calls the other side vendidos, sellouts, which makes enemies of men he needs.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep the commons and the county seat, and to prove that a plaza schoolmaster can beat a railroad company. Now also to keep his sister's boy from being hanged.

npcsInvolved.name: Rafael Candelaria, 22
npcsInvolved.role: The relief driver, on the roof; Jethro's apprentice (companion)
npcsInvolved.description: See his sheet. Jethro taught him to drive, and he would do anything for him except lie under oath, which he is about to find out.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To drive the line's coach, and to marry Don Fermín Lucero's granddaughter.

npcsInvolved.name: Sheriff Florencio Jaramillo, 56
npcsInvolved.role: Sheriff of Rio Seco County, at the plaza
npcsInvolved.description: A heavy grey man, slow-spoken, a sheep rancher who has been sheriff for eight years and is liked because he is fair. He has two deputies, a jail of two cells and no money. He is a People's man, but he will arrest anyone the evidence points at.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep the peace, keep Paragon's men out of his county seat, and not start a war he cannot finish.

npcsInvolved.name: Justice Anacleto Lovato, 70
npcsInvolved.role: Justice of the peace, Santa Teresita
npcsInvolved.description: A small slow old man in a black coat who writes one word at a time and blots each. Cautious and honest. He records only what is proved.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To write down the truth, no more and no less, and to die without having been anyone's man.

npcsInvolved.name: Fenton Rusk, 50
npcsInvolved.role: The Company's election agent; the man who planned the robbery
npcsInvolved.description: Plump, pleasant, beautifully barbered, with a straw boater, a gold watch-chain and a voice that makes you feel he has been waiting all day to meet you. A Santa Fe fixer who has run elections in four counties and never lost one. He listens more than he talks and writes things in a little book.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To win the county seat for the Company, which will make him rich, and never to be connected to anything that happened at the Puerto de Piedra.

npcsInvolved.name: Everard Coldiron, 44
npcsInvolved.role: Manager of the Paragon Townsite & Improvement Company
npcsInvolved.description: Lean, handsome, clean-shaven, with a fine tenor voice and real faith in the town he is building. He gives short good speeches about progress. He has made a point of not knowing how Rusk will win.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To make Paragon the county seat and the commons the Company's, and to report to St. Louis that he did it by the book.

npcsInvolved.name: Constable Ott Ebner, 40
npcsInvolved.description: A big red-faced Iowan with a nickel star, a new hat and a temper. He believes the poster. He is not a killer, and two of the men he brings with him are.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be somebody in a town that is going to be somebody. To arrest the bandits and be thanked for it.

npcsInvolved.name: Cade Rendell, 38
npcsInvolved.role: Texas gunman; the man who shot Lon Brisbane
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, fair, sun-reddened, with pale eyes and a soft voice, a Sharps buffalo rifle in a fringed case and an ivory-handled Army revolver. Rode with Royal Penhallow's gang in Kansas in 1876 and was the one who got away. He plans everything twice and is vain of his reputation.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His money, and one famous gunfight before he leaves the territory. He doesn't care about the election at all.

npcsInvolved.name: Hob Linnet, 33
npcsInvolved.role: Rendell's man; carries the notes to Paragon
npcsInvolved.description: Heavy, slow, sunburned and frightened of Rendell. He was a teamster until he wasn't. If caught, he is the gang's weak link.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His $500, and to get out of the territory alive.

npcsInvolved.name: Victoriano Romero, 44, of Laguna Pueblo
npcsInvolved.role: Section foreman on the railroad at Paragon; a witness
npcsInvolved.description: A compact, grey-templed man in a railroad cap and a good wool coat, who speaks Keres, Spanish and English, runs his section gang well and is respected by both towns. He works on the line under his pueblo's agreement with the railroad, and he is watching the Company for Laguna's own reasons.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His pueblo's interest, which in this scenario is simply to know what the Company is doing near Laguna's boundary. He tells the truth to people who treat him as what he is.

npcsInvolved.name: Hosea Durrant, 50
npcsInvolved.role: Smith at the Paragon Livery & Feed
npcsInvolved.description: A quiet Englishman from Shropshire with burned forearms and a careful book. He shoes with factory shoes because the Company buys them, and he despises them.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep his job and his conscience, in that order until this week.

rewards.money: Cyprian Ludlow pays nothing, because he has nothing, but stands the party the dinner he promised and gives each of them a lifetime pass on a line that no longer runs. The Southwestern Express Company's agent in Albuquerque, Milo Thackery, wires a standing reward: $500 for the box and its contents, $250 for each robber, payable on conviction. Sheriff Jaramillo offers deputy's badges at $2 a day in county scrip. The Committee's $1,000 for Tiburcio is there for anyone who wants it. Anything taken from Hob Linnet (the $6,000 in notes, if the party catches him, and $40 of his own) is evidence.
items: The waybill and the serial-number schedule (CLUE C1)
Tiburcio's sombrero with T.A. in the band (CLUE A5)
The Paragon Mercantile cartridge box and a .50 cartridge case from the ridge (CLUES A3, A4)
The red rag from the juniper (CLUE F1)
A copy of the $1,000 poster and Friday's Paragon Pioneer, with or without 'Mexican bandits'
A lifetime pass on the Rio Seco Mail & Stage Line, signed C. Ludlow

twists: If the party keeps the box at the Puerto de Piedra, let them. Lon is still dead, the Committee still has Tiburcio's sombrero and still posts the reward, and Rusk falls back on the Company's own cash for the miners' envelopes. That means old notes, so there are no serial numbers, but the envelopes were still ordered on 20 June (CLUE C3) and are now the case's spine. Rendell, cheated of the box, is more dangerous and goes after Jethro at once, for talking.

If the party catches Hob Linnet with the notes, Rusk has no stolen money to spend, and pays the repeaters and the miners from Coldiron's safe in the Company's own notes. That puts the Company's money in the plot directly, which Coldiron hates. Linnet in custody is a witness Rendell must kill. Expect an attempt on the plaza jail on the night of Monday 4 July.

Rusk is the most helpful man the party meets in Paragon. He offers to share the Committee's information, introduces them to Coldiron, and suggests that strangers with the plaza's coach might help the Committee 'avoid a misunderstanding' by bringing the boy in themselves for the reward. Every helpful thing he does is a way of finding out what they know. If they mention the serial numbers, he changes notes that night.

Tiburcio rode west to the Ojo del Gato and Rufina Sedillo's sheep camp. A party that follows the cow pony on Thursday night finds him by midnight, hysterical and soaked in sweat, with a pistol he doesn't know how to use pointed at them. If they talk him down he tells them everything (CLUE A5) and begs them not to take him to the plaza. Getting him hidden and keeping him alive is st-scenario-002's first problem, a day earlier than it would otherwise be.
dmTips: This scenario sets up the coach, the factions, the mystery and the clock. Budget an hour for Wednesday and the Puerco station, an hour for the robbery and the arroyo, and an hour and a half for Friday to Sunday. The only expected fight is the robbery. The Cañoncito and Linnet's ride are optional, and very rewarding.

Lon Brisbane has to die, and it should hurt. Give him the whole of Wednesday: the Bible verses, the drummer's deck, the psalm at the Puerco station. Then the robbery's first sound is the shot that kills him. Tell the players afterwards, if they ask, that it was not something they could have stopped. It was decided before they boarded, and the man who decided it is in Paragon.

The robbery is not a trap the party is supposed to fail. Rendell's plan is good, and they can still win pieces of it. Reward initiative generously: a player who gets under the coach and shoots the man coming up for the box has changed the campaign. The box going down the arroyo is the default, not a law.

Spanish matters in this campaign. The robbers' Spanish is the first clue, and the players who speak it, or whose characters do, should hear it as wrong. If no one at the table does, Celestino will say it for them on the road: 'That was no man of the plaza. That was a Texan.'
The sombrero is a gift to whoever plays Nicanor. It is his brother's. Let the player decide whether to tell anyone, hide it or burn it, and let that choice follow him.

Don't let Paragon be a town of villains. Durrant the smith, the hotel clerk, the band, most of the Committee and Constable Ebner himself believe the poster. They are wrong, not wicked. Rusk is the only one who knows, and he is the nicest man in town.

The President's shooting on 2 July is real history, and it is the news that closes Saturday night in both towns. Let the telegraph bring it to Paragon. Let a rider bring it to the plaza, where the priest rings the bell and both towns, for one evening, worry about the same thing.

End with Lon's funeral on Sunday and a list of what the party knows. If they have the serial numbers, the shoes and the register, they are ahead of Rusk and don't yet know it. Then summarise Sunday night: the Company's buckboard at the plaza with the mail, already opened and resealed, and Jethro Petree sitting alone on the coach's box in the dark corral.
